text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000172 bills 99215 far above expected in every complexity band, but the few returned charts mostly support the billed level, so the pattern is not yet resolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 billing is not explained by panel acuity, since the 99215 share runs well above the all-provider rate in the 0–4 condition bands. Some low-complexity 99215s look hard to justify on the claim alone, such as C0087246 (no chronic conditions, UTI diagnosis), C0087379 (Z09 follow-up only) and C0087318 (the one documented 99215 found below level). Against that, 12 of 13 documented 99215s supported the billed level, including high-MDM examples like C0087054 and C0087069, which points toward legitimate complexity; the 99214 below-level rate is also somewhat elevated, though on very small counts. That support is weakened by thin records (about 8% of claims), a notable share of duplicate and repeated-time notes that could reflect cloned documentation, and no audit trail to test whether notes were bulk-created or edited. A reviewer should first pull charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and request the EHR audit trail to check whether the duplicate or time-repeat notes were templated to match the billed level."}
